cases.question: How often do residents appeal automated municipal benefit decisions, and how does the rate vary by service channel?
cases.population: Completed automated benefit decisions in participating municipalities
cases.samplingPlan: Enumerate eligible decisions and report coverage and missingness by municipality
cases.measurementPlan: Define appeal, channel, denominator, missing values, and duplicate decisions before extraction
cases.dataCollectionPlan: Import de-identified decision and appeal records under documented access rules
cases.analysisPlan: Report counts, rates, uncertainty intervals, and missingness without causal interpretation
cases.preanalysisPlan: Freeze eligibility, variables, denominators, exclusions, and subgroup tables before extraction
feasibilityLimits: No claim about residents who never initiated an application
cases.ethicsNote: Confirm lawful access and de-identification before import
cases.decisionLimitation: Administrative records do not measure unfiled grievances
cases.basisSummary: The fixture represents a descriptive design with an explicit evidence gap

cases.question: How is the quality of algorithmic explanations associated with institutional trust among service users?
cases.method: Panel survey with declared covariate adjustment
cases.population: Residents who received an automated municipal service decision
cases.samplingPlan: Recruit from documented service-user frames and report attrition by wave
cases.measurementPlan: Use preregistered explanation-quality and institutional-trust scales
cases.dataCollectionPlan: Collect consented surveys linked by pseudonymous respondent IDs
cases.analysisPlan: Estimate within-person associations with declared controls and robustness checks
cases.preanalysisPlan: Freeze scales, exclusions, covariates, models, and robustness checks before outcome analysis
alternativeExplanations: Prior service satisfaction may influence both perceived explanation quality and trust
boundaryConditions: Resident-facing municipal algorithms with an explanation interface
feasibilityLimits: Association is not interpreted as an intervention effect
cases.ethicsNote: Collect consent and minimize linkage fields
cases.basisSummary: The fixture tests explicit separation of association from causality

cases.question: What is the effect of a staggered explanation mandate on successful appeals of automated licensing decisions?
cases.population: Licensing decisions in adopting and not-yet-adopting municipalities
cases.timeframe: 24 months before through 18 months after adoption
cases.samplingPlan: Include municipalities with stable reporting and document adoption timing exclusions
cases.measurementPlan: Predefine mandate adoption, appeal success, exposure windows, and reporting completeness
cases.dataCollectionPlan: Import versioned municipal policy dates and de-identified aggregate outcomes
cases.analysisPlan: Estimate event-time effects with municipality and month fixed effects, clustered uncertainty, and pretrend diagnostics
cases.identificationStrategy: Compare outcome changes for adopters with not-yet-adopters under staggered timing
identificationAssumptions: Parallel untreated trends conditional on declared controls
cases.preanalysisPlan: Freeze estimand, cohort handling, event window, controls, standard errors, diagnostics, and placebo tests
boundaryConditions: Municipalities with comparable licensing and reporting systems
feasibilityLimits: Causal interpretation is blocked if adoption timing or pretrend diagnostics fail
cases.ethicsNote: Use aggregate outcomes and review small-cell disclosure risk
cases.decisionLimitation: Policy timing may coincide with other reforms
cases.basisSummary: The fixture permits causal language only under explicit identification assumptions

cases.question: How do frontline workers understand responsibility when they review algorithmic recommendations?
cases.method: Semi-structured interviews with reflexive thematic analysis
cases.population: Frontline workers who review algorithmic recommendations
cases.samplingPlan: Use maximum-variation purposive sampling across roles and tenure
cases.measurementPlan: Define responsibility, discretion, and review episodes in a versioned coding memo
cases.dataCollectionPlan: Record consented interviews and retain redacted transcripts with stable locators
cases.analysisPlan: Apply a versioned codebook, preserve negative cases, and record researcher decisions
cases.interviewPlan: Pilot a semi-structured guide, obtain consent, and document interviewer and context effects
alternativeExplanations: Formal job role may shape accounts independently of algorithm use
boundaryConditions: Organizations where human review remains formally available
feasibilityLimits: Accounts do not establish behavioral frequency or causal effects
cases.ethicsNote: Protect employment identity and voluntary participation
cases.decisionLimitation: Self-reports may differ from observed practice
cases.basisSummary: The fixture defines an interpretive target and preserves an evidence gap

cases.question: How do different procurement arrangements shape municipal oversight of algorithm vendors?
cases.population: Municipal algorithm procurement and oversight arrangements
cases.timeframe: Procurement through the first two operating years
cases.samplingPlan: Select contrasting arrangements using declared procurement and oversight dimensions
cases.measurementPlan: Operationalize oversight authority, information access, sanctions, and escalation paths
cases.dataCollectionPlan: Collect public contracts, oversight records, and consented key-informant interviews
cases.analysisPlan: Apply the same questions across cases and preserve within-case and cross-case evidence matrices
cases.interviewPlan: Use role-specific guides and document nonresponse
cases.caseSelectionPlan: Select cases with variation in procurement form while documenting contextual differences
alternativeExplanations: Municipal legal capacity may explain oversight differences
boundaryConditions: Municipal procurements with observable oversight records
feasibilityLimits: Small purposive samples limit population generalization
cases.ethicsNote: Separate public documents from consented interview material
cases.decisionLimitation: Case comparability depends on record availability
cases.basisSummary: The fixture makes case-selection logic and alternatives explicit

cases.question: Did an independent audit trigger the replacement of a discriminatory eligibility model in one municipality?
cases.population: Decision episodes surrounding the model replacement
cases.samplingPlan: Collect all accessible decision episodes and purposively seek evidence for rival explanations
cases.measurementPlan: Predefine observable implications for audit influence, legal pressure, leadership change, and vendor failure
cases.dataCollectionPlan: Triangulate dated public records with consented interviews and preserve source locators
cases.analysisPlan: Sequence events, test predicted observations, and grade evidence separately for the focal and rival mechanisms
cases.identificationStrategy: Within-case causal-process tests using temporal order, mechanism evidence, and explicit rival-explanation tests
identificationAssumptions: Key decision records are not systematically missing
Interview accounts are triangulated rather than accepted alone
cases.interviewPlan: Interview participants from audit, legal, program, and vendor roles with consent and contradiction checks
cases.caseSelectionPlan: Select the case because the audit and replacement are observable, not because the focal mechanism is already proven
boundaryConditions: Single municipal replacement episode with reconstructable timing
feasibilityLimits: Causal conclusion remains case-specific and depends on mechanism evidence
cases.ethicsNote: Redact identifiable employment and whistleblower details
cases.decisionLimitation: Missing private deliberations may leave mechanisms underdetermined
cases.basisSummary: The fixture permits a bounded causal inference only through explicit process evidence
